definitions.explanation: The twentieth day of any month.

examples.japanese: {二十日|はつか}ぐらいかかる。
{二十日|はつか}{間|かん}{休|やす}みを{取|と}った。
{工事|こうじ}は{二十日|はつか}で{終|お}わる{予定|よてい}です。
examples.english: The construction is scheduled to be completed in twenty days.

examples.japanese: {薬|くすり}を{二十日|はつか}{分|ぶん}もらったので、{来月|らいげつ}まで{足|た}りるはずだ。
examples.english: I received twenty days' worth of medicine, so it should last until next month.

examples.japanese: {一月|いちがつ}{二十日|はつか}
{二十日|はつか}に{届|とど}きます。
{二十日|はつか}までにお{届|とど}けします。
examples.english: We will deliver it by the 20th.

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}の{二十日|はつか}に{会議|かいぎ}がある。
examples.english: There is a meeting on the 20th of next month.

examples.japanese: {二十日|はつか}は{祝日|しゅくじつ}なので、{学校|がっこう}も{会社|かいしゃ}も{休|やす}みです。
examples.english: The 20th is a holiday, so both school and work are off.

notes:
{二十日|はつか} has two uses: "twenty days" (a duration) and "the 20th" (a date). The reading はつか is irregular and must be memorized.

SPECIAL DAY READINGS (1st-10th):
Days 1-10 of the month all have unique native Japanese readings: {一日|ついたち}, {二日|ふつか}, {三日|みっか}, {四日|よっか}, {五日|いつか}, {六日|むいか}, {七日|なのか}, {八日|ようか}, {九日|ここのか}, {十日|とおか}.

AFTER THE 10TH:
Most days use Sino-Japanese numbers + {日|にち} (e.g., {十一日|じゅういちにち}), but a few retain special readings:
- {十四日|じゅうよっか} (14th)
- {二十日|はつか} (20th)
- {二十四日|にじゅうよっか} (24th)

COMMON COMPOUND:
- {二十日|はつか}{大根|だいこん}: small Japanese radish (literally "20-day radish" because it matures quickly)
